title: quote_v1
description: One real person's real words, with the basis on which we may show them. A quote is an ATTRIBUTED OPINION in ADR-001's sense: the fact is that they said it, the opinion is theirs, and the decision to display it belongs to the consumer. This repository never anonymises a quote and never invents one; both of those failures have already shipped here (pdoom-data#92, #76).

id.description: Stable forever. A person asking years later to correct, re-attribute or withdraw their words must be executable against this id without re-deriving which line in the game is theirs.

text.description: Verbatim. Never paraphrased, never trimmed in a way that changes the sense. If it needs an ellipsis, the ellipsis is part of the text.

is_pseudonym.description: True when only a handle is known. A pseudonymous private commenter gets the MOST diligence, not the least: they chose not to attach their name to this, and a game screen re-attaches it to a context they never saw.

identification_attempts.description: What was actually done to reach the person behind a pseudonym. Required in practice before any pseudonymous quote is served.

display_preference.description: How they asked to be credited, in their words. Overrides name for display.

archive_url.description: Wayback or equivalent, captured AT RETRIEVAL TIME. Forum posts get edited and deleted; without this the quote becomes unverifiable and we cannot prove we quoted it correctly.

published_at.description: ISO date the source was published. Load-bearing for ea_forum: CC BY 4.0 is mandatory only from 2022-12-01. Earlier posts are ordinary copyright unless that author added a licence clause to that post.

context_note.description: What the person was actually talking about. Guards against context collapse (Marwick and boyd 2011): a 2018 forum comment on a 2026 death screen has lost its audience, its thread and possibly the author's current view.

basis.description: not_yet_asked is the DEFAULT and is an absence, not a permission. asked_no_reply is also not permission: silence means no. refused and withdrawn are permanent tombstones.

licence_spdx.description: Required when basis is licence. Checked mechanically: anything containing -SA is refused, per the standing rule that share-alike would reach into this project's own licensing. NC and ND are refused too, because the game is a commercial product.

granted_by.description: The person who said yes, named. Required when basis is granted.

granted_via.description: Email, DM, or wherever. A grant we cannot point at is not a grant.

context_shown_to_author.description: What we told them about WHERE it would appear. Consent is to a context, not just to a reuse, so a grant obtained without describing the death screen is not a grant for the death screen.

refused_note.description: Kept so a refusal cannot be silently reversed by someone who never saw it. A refused quote stays in this file, unservable, forever.

placements.description: Which in-game surfaces this was cleared for. A grant for a loading screen is not a grant for a death screen.

quote_kind.description: What the quote is DOING. 'difficulty' is the Call of Duty shape: the player lost, and here is someone saying why this problem is genuinely hard. 'accountability' places a named public figure's own words beside what later happened. They carry different risk and the gate treats them differently: an accountability quote must be verified against a primary source, must carry the dated evidence of the outcome it is set against, and its framing may not assert what the speaker knew or intended.

speaker_status.description: An executive speaking publicly about their own company is not the same as a forum commenter, legally or ethically. Required for accountability quotes.

against_primary_source.description: Checked against the original recording, transcript or filing, NOT against someone else's report of the quote. A misquote repeated accurately is still a misquote, and this repo has already run one primary-source pass that refuted six claims, four of them high confidence.

full_context_url.description: Where a player or a subject can read the WHOLE thing. The defence against a cropping accusation is that the crop is one click from the original.

juxtaposition.description: For accountability quotes: what happened afterwards, evidenced. The player draws the inference; the game does not draw it for them. This is both the stronger rhetoric and the safer position.

what_happened.description: Dated, factual, and checkable. An event, not a characterisation.

evidence_urls.description: At least one. The outcome carries its own evidence, exactly as every date in config/sources.json does.

framing_text.description: Any words the GAME says around the quote, in its own voice. This is the actual risk surface: reproducing what someone said is one thing, and asserting what they knew or intended is another. Checked mechanically.

right_of_reply.description: REQUIRED for accountability quotes, and not out of courtesy. In Russell v Australian Broadcasting Corporation (No 3) [2023] FCA 1223, the first full trial of the s 29A public interest defence, the ABC's defence FAILED and it paid over AUD 400,000. Lee J accepted the ABC honestly believed publication was in the public interest but found the belief unreasonable, decisively because it did not seek and fairly consider a response from the subject. A declined or ignored request still counts, PROVIDED it is documented. Silence from them is fine; silence from us is not.

their_response.description: Verbatim if they gave one. Carrying their answer beside the quote is worth more than any framing we could write.

sources_shown_in_product.description: Whether the source and the evidence are VISIBLE TO THE PLAYER beside the quote, not merely recorded in this file. The s 31 honest opinion defence requires the opinion to rest on 'proper material' that is stated or referenced in the same publication, by link or other access point. Evidence held in a repository the player never sees does not satisfy it. This is a UI requirement that only the data can record.

editorial_note.description: Why this quote, why this juxtaposition, and what was checked. The s 29A defence turns on whether the belief that publication served the public interest was REASONABLE, which is judged on what was actually done. A contemporaneous record of the decision is the evidence of that, and it cannot be reconstructed afterwards.
